description: After a missed magic attack the Confliction gauntlets make the next magic attack of that weapon or spell against the same enemy roll accuracy twice, so the effect has memory and is priced by the wiki's steady-state hit chance built from the one-roll and two-roll probabilities; outside the Tombs the two attack rolls share one defence roll, so the two-roll term is the correlated closed form. The effect is disabled with a two-handed weapon, which is what excludes Tumeken's shadow, and on a multi-target cast only the primary target gets the double roll, so a clumped cast is the target-count-weighted mean. A worn brimstone ring is folded into both rolls here rather than composed afterwards, since its proc is rolled per attack; the PvP ice-spell exclusion is not modelled.

description: The twisted bow scales accuracy and damage off the higher of the target's Magic level and Magic attack bonus, by the two published quadratics clamped to 140% and 250%, with every division truncated. Accuracy is its own late, separately floored stage while damage folds into the main product with the other Ranged bonuses; below Magic level 4 the additive term's numerator is negative and the wiki states no rounding direction there, so the row follows the truncation the rest of the formula uses.

accuracy.factor: clamp(140 + idiv(3 * min(player.inCoX ? 350 : 250, max(monster.magicLevel, monster.magicAttackBonus)) - 10, 100) - idiv(pow(idiv(3 * min(player.inCoX ? 350 : 250, max(monster.magicLevel, monster.magicAttackBonus)), 10) - 100, 2), 100), 0, 140) / 100

Roll accuracy. If successful, roll total damage between 75% and 175% of the maximum hit. Divide the damage into three hitsplats as 25%-25%-50%.

If first roll misses, reroll accuracy. If successful, roll total damage between 50% and 150% of the maximum hit. Divide the damage into three hitsplats as 50%-50%-0%, then subtract 1 from the first two hitsplats and add that damage to the third hitsplat

description: The dragon halberd's Sweep special attack lands a second hitsplat against monsters larger than one tile, at 25% reduced accuracy; halberds reach two tiles, which is what puts them in range of such targets. The engine applies the reduction to the attack roll and re-derives hit chance from it, and folds the second hit into the accuracy sum so that accuracy times expected damage stays exact. The wiki's wording does not separate a three quarter attack roll from a three quarter hit chance, so the roll-level reading is a pinned assumption; the damage bonus is already carried in the max hit.

quotes: they have an attack range of two tiles
if used against "large" monsters (anything that is larger than 1x1, such as most Boss monsters), the special attack will deal an additional second hit onto them, although with 25% reduced accuracy

description: The Saradomin sword's special attack deals 10% more melee damage plus 1 to 16 extra Magic damage. The magic bolt rolls no accuracy of its own and fails when the melee hit misses, and against targets immune to magic damage it lands for zero. The melee half's multiplier is an ordinary chain stage, and flat armour never applies to magic damage.

quotes: deals 10% more melee damage and 1-16 extra Magic damage

description: Enchanted ruby bolts trigger Blood Forfeit on 6% of shots in PvM, dealing 20% of the target's current hitpoints capped at 100 damage, so the proc decays over a kill and is averaged across it by a closed form. The proc overrides the ordinary projectile damage, so a proc shot pays the proc instead of the normal hit and the addend is the difference of expectations. Against the Gemstone Crab the boss is treated as having a fixed 300 hitpoints for 60 damage, 66 with a Zaryte crossbow, so nothing decays; the Hard Kandarin Diary raises the chance while the Zaryte raises the damage, and that damage scale is divided by the hitsplat scale because the Corporeal Beast halving happens before the 100 cap while the engine scales the whole addend afterwards.

quotes: The special effect has a 11% chance of activating in PvP and a 6% chance of activating in PvM
damage dealt to the target will be 20% of the opponent's current Hitpoints with a cap of 100 damage
overrides the projectile's damage

with enchanted ruby bolts, the bolt's special effect, Blood Forfeit, would deal 22% of the opponent's current hitpoints with a cap of 110 damage, rather than the usual 20% damage and 100 hitpoints damage cap
Ruby bolt (e) special attacks treat the boss as if it has 300 Hitpoints and deal 60 damage, increased to 66 if using a Zaryte crossbow
before the cap of 100 damage is calculated

description: Enchanted diamond bolts trigger Armour Piercing on 10% of shots, raising the maximum damage by 15%, or 26% under a Zaryte crossbow, and guaranteeing the hit lands. Those shots replace the ordinary one, so the addend is the difference of expectations. No bound is claimed, because the widened roll's ceiling scales with the loadout's max hit rather than any chunk constant.

quotes: Diamond bolts (e) have a 10% chance (5% chance against another player) of triggering the Armour Piercing effect.
This increases the maximum damage by 15% (26% when under the effect of the Zaryte crossbow) for that hit and guarantees it will be a successful hit.

description: Enchanted onyx bolts trigger Life Leech on 11% of landed hits in PvM, replacing the hit with a roll up to 120% of max hit, or 132% under a Zaryte crossbow. The effect does not work on the undead, which the row excludes. No bound is claimed, because roll widening has no chunk-constant ceiling.

quotes: The special effect has a 10% chance of activating in PvP and an 11% chance of activating in PvM
This will deal 20% extra damage (32% when under the effect of the Zaryte crossbow)
This does not work on the undead, as they have no 'life' to leech.
Max hit is increased from 120% of normal max to 132%

description: Enchanted dragonstone bolts trigger Dragon's breath on 6% of landed hits, adding damage equal to 20% of the attacker's visible Ranged level rounded down, or 22% under a Zaryte crossbow. The Zaryte crossbow page states the dragonstone enhancement as a percentage where it states opal's and pearl's as divisors, so the engine uses 22/100 rather than 2/9. The effect does not activate against targets immune to dragonfire, an immunity that requires the opponent to be both fiery and draconic.

quotes: Dragonstone bolts (e) have a 6% chance of triggering the Dragon's breath effect upon a successful hit. This inflicts a dragonfire against the target, adding extra damage to a bolt hit equal to 20% of the attacker's visible Ranged level, rounded down.
Slightly more extra damage is done if under the passive effect of the Zaryte crossbow (22% instead of 20%). If the target is immune to dragonfire, the special effect will not activate.
Dragonfire damage is increased from [visible ranged * 20%] to [visible ranged * 22%].
These methods will not cause damage if the opponent is both a fiery and draconic creature

description: Enchanted pearl bolts trigger Sea Curse on 6% of shots, adding a twentieth of the user's visible Ranged level, raised to a fifteenth against fiery enemies. The chance is rolled whether or not the shot lands. A Zaryte crossbow takes two off the divisor in either case.

quotes: Enchanted pearl bolts have a 6% chance to trigger the Sea Curse effect
Against fiery enemies, the increase is boosted to 1/15 of the user's Ranged level. Against other targets, the increase is 1/20 of the user's Ranged level.
Added damage is increased from [visible ranged / 15] to [visible ranged / 13] for fiery targets; [visible ranged / 20] to [visible ranged / 18] for all others.

description: Enchanted opal bolts trigger Lucky Lightning on 5% of shots, adding a tenth of the visible Ranged level rounded down; the chance is rolled whether or not the shot passes its accuracy roll. A Zaryte crossbow takes one off the divisor.

quotes: Opal bolts (e) have a chance (5%) of triggering the Lucky Lightning effect, which results in a lightning bolt striking your opponent and causing extra damage (visible ranged level/10). When under the effect of the Zaryte crossbow, this damage is scaled up slightly (visible ranged level/9).
regardless of whether or not it passes an accuracy roll

description: Enchanted emerald bolts poison the target on 55% of landed hits, for 75 total damage, or 87 with a Zaryte crossbow, paid out every 30 ticks starting at 5 damage per interval, 6 at the Zaryte's higher severity. Because a re-applying weapon can reset the duration on an already poisoned enemy while the interval timer stays with the NPC, the opening damage is held indefinitely, so the contribution is the lesser of what the procs deliver and what the poison can pay out, converted to a per-shot average through the attack time the engine divides by rather than the base speed. Nothing is contributed against poison-immune targets.

quotes: Emerald bolts (e) have a 55% (54% against other players) chance of triggering the Magical Poison effect.
If used with a Zaryte crossbow, the initial poison severity will be increased from 5 to 6.
The total poison damage dealt by a single emerald bolt proc is 75 health points over 7.5 minutes. With the Zaryte crossbow, this is increased to 87 over 8.1 minutes
every 30 game ticks (18 seconds)
The poison's duration can be reset while the enemy is poisoned with the same chance as on an unpoisoned enemy

description: Chinchompas explode on impact and hit up to 11 targets in a 3x3 area in PvM, 12 for black chinchompas, and the reported number above one target is DPS across the clump. One accuracy roll on the primary target covers the whole group, which changes variance rather than expectation, and secondary targets lose the salve and avarice boosts while keeping the black mask, which is why the ratio reads those two multipliers apart. Not modelled: cleave and bounce weapons, PvP target caps, and whether the enemies are really stacked.

quotes: In PvM, they can hit up to 11 targets in a 3x3 area.
the accuracy roll is based on the targeted NPC. If you miss on this target, you will miss on all targets. If you hit on this target, you will hit on all targets.
the max hit used for the damage roll on the additional targets is the max hit for the initial target with the boosts from Salve and Avarice removed
In PvM, they can hit up to 12 (as opposed to 11 with other chinchompas) targets in a 3x3 area.
